grants.Total Funding: Up to $787,000,000, combining FYs 2024, 2025, and 2026 funding in a single competition, plus any unobligated PROTECT Competitive funding remaining from prior years.

grants.Program Focus:
Improves the resilience of the surface transportation system — highways, public transportation, ports, and intercity passenger rail. Stated program goals are protecting surface transportation assets by making them more resilient; protecting communities through resilience improvements and strategies enabling continued operation or rapid recovery; protecting coastal infrastructure; and protecting natural infrastructure that shields and enhances surface transportation assets.

The NOFO covers two application tracks: Planning, Resilience Improvement, and Community Resilience and Evacuation Route Grants; and At-Risk Coastal Infrastructure Grants. Separate application templates are posted for the planning and resilience tracks.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Yes — non-federal cost share required. Share requirements (0-20%) vary by grant type and by the resilience planning status of the applicant.

grants.Description: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service — Assisting Specialty Crop Exports: Low Oxygen Storage and Packaging Systems for U.S. Tree Nuts with Phytosanitary Traceability
grants.Opportunity #: USDA-FAS-10621-0750-106-27-0001; Assistance Listing 10.621 (Assisting Specialty Crop Exports). Grants.gov opportunity 363690.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Agriculture — Foreign Agricultural Service
grants.Award Range: $2,000,000 maximum; one award anticipated at the full program amount. There is no partial-award path.
grants.Eligible Applicants: This opportunity is available to U.S. academic institutions, state governments, nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) designation, U.S. trade associations, U.S. agricultural cooperatives, international organizations, foreign entities, and any other entity including private sector businesses.
grants.Program Focus:
Tree nut handlers increasingly use modified or controlled atmosphere storage holding oxygen below 1% by volume. Low-oxygen conditions control insect pests, leave no chemical residue, and suppress the lipid oxidation that causes rancidity — but there is currently no efficient way for a shipper to validate those conditions to a customer, let alone to an importing government with phytosanitary requirements.

Existing low-oxygen technologies do not incorporate digital mapping or official record-keeping during packing and storage, so there is no non-invasive method to verify oxygen content over time inside gas-impermeable liners or to confirm seal integrity. The program funds development of technically and economically viable, verifiable, and preferably traceable technology to close that gap.

The trade context is concrete: India, Korea, and Japan require phytosanitary treatment such as fumigation for post-harvest pest management before many U.S. tree nuts may be imported, and buyers in other markets request treatment as a condition of sale. Fumigation and freezing are both expensive and create marketing bottlenecks.
grants.Primary Sector: Tree Nuts (almond, walnut, pistachio); Post-Harvest Technology; Controlled and Modified Atmosphere Storage; Phytosanitary Compliance and Traceability; Agricultural Export Market Access; Sensor and Digital Monitoring Systems

grants.Description: NOAA Fisheries, Southeast Fisheries Science Center — Bluefin Tuna Research Program, FY 2027
grants.Opportunity #: NOAA-NMFS-FHQ-2027-33398; Assistance Listing 11.452 (Unallied Industry Projects). Grants.gov opportunity 363692.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Commerce — NOAA, National Marine Fisheries Service, Office of Sustainable Fisheries
grants.Award Range: $50,000 minimum to $400,000 maximum; approximately 30 awards anticipated.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Individuals, institutions of higher education, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and state, local, U.S. territorial, Alaska Native, and Tribal governments. Federal agencies and instrumentalities are not eligible.

The program is framed around non-federal researchers working to benefit U.S. fishermen — fishing industry participants and gear manufacturers are squarely within the intended applicant pool, not just academic institutions.
grants.Program Focus:
Established under 16 U.S.C. 1865 of the Magnuson-Stevens Act, which requires NOAA conservation and management measures to minimize bycatch to the extent practicable. Funds development and testing of technological devices and conservation engineering changes that minimize bycatch and reduce post-release mortality of non-target species in commercial and recreational fisheries, including aquaculture.

Bycatch reduction is a stated NMFS priority under the National Bycatch Reduction Strategy. The framing in the announcement is practical rather than theoretical: bycatch contributes to overfishing, drives population declines for threatened and endangered species, and can trigger commercial fishery closures.
grants.Primary Sector: Conservation Engineering; Fishing Gear Technology; Bycatch and Post-Release Mortality; Protected Species Interactions; Commercial and Recreational Fisheries; Aquaculture
grants.Link to NOFO: BREP on Simpler.Grants.gov; NOAA-NMFS-FHQ-2027-33398 Full Announcement (PDF); NMFS National Bycatch Reduction Strategy

grants.Description: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service — FY2026 Implementation of the Quagga and Zebra Mussel Action Plan (QZAP) in the Western United States
grants.Opportunity #: F26AS00105; Assistance Listing 15.685 (National Fish Passage). Grants.gov opportunity 363699.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of the Interior — Fish and Wildlife Service
grants.Total Funding: $15,000,000, appropriated by the Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026. Of that, $5,000,000 is designated for projects implementing the Fisheries Restoration and Irrigation Mitigation Act (FRIMA), Pub. L. 106-502.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000 per award, with no meaningful floor; approximately 100 awards anticipated.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Unrestricted. The program develops projects collaboratively with partners including state and local agencies, Tribes, non-governmental organizations, other federal agencies, and private landowners.

Additional requirements and geographic restrictions apply to the FRIMA set-aside; those are defined in the announcement and on the program website rather than in the general eligibility statement.
grants.Deadline: April 30, 2027, 11:59 PM Eastern. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Interested applicants should reach out to their local or regional NFPP coordinator for more information and deadlines. Informal award notice is given before recipients are invited to apply via GrantSolutions.
grants.Program Focus:
Provides technical and financial assistance to remove instream barriers and restore aquatic connectivity, improve community safety, and support local economies. Typical projects include removal of obsolete and dangerous infrastructure, culvert replacement, floodplain restoration, and fishway installation. FWS estimates $1.5 million in economic value added per $1 million invested.

Delivery is through Service field offices nationwide. Local Service staff work with partners to identify and develop projects, and the announcement directs applicants to contact the regional NFPP Coordinator for program priorities and application process.
grants.Primary Sector: Aquatic Connectivity; Dam and Barrier Removal; Culvert Replacement and Road-Stream Crossings; Floodplain Restoration; Salmonid Habitat; Community Flood Risk Reduction; Tribal Natural Resources
grants.Link to NOFO: National Fish Passage Program on Simpler.Grants.gov; F26AS00105 Full Announcement (PDF); Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service — Cooperative Endangered Species Conservation Fund: Habitat Conservation Plan Land Acquisition Grants
grants.Opportunity #: F26AS00071; Assistance Listing 15.615 (Cooperative Endangered Species Conservation Fund). Grants.gov opportunity 363691.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of the Interior — Fish and Wildlife Service
grants.Award Range: $10,000 minimum to $26,000,000 maximum; approximately 10 awards anticipated.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
State and territorial agencies only, and only those that have entered into a cooperative agreement under section 6(c) of the Endangered Species Act and have supplied the information needed for annual renewal of that agreement.

Counties, conservation organizations, and land trusts participate as subgrantees working with an eligible State agency — they cannot apply directly. In California that means the California Department of Fish and Wildlife is the applicant of record for any project a local partner wants funded.
grants.Program Focus:
Created by Congress in FY 1997 to reduce conflict between conservation of listed species and competing land uses on specific parcels associated with approved and permitted Habitat Conservation Plans. FWS provides matching grants to State agencies for land acquisition that conserves species habitat in perpetuity, through fee simple purchase or permanent conservation easement.

Land proposed for acquisition must benefit at least one federally listed species included on an active section 10(a)(1)(B) permit. Parcels must be individually identified on the SF-429 and SF-429-B to be eligible, though they may be grouped at the property or transaction level for evaluation. Where specific properties are not yet identified, an applicant may describe an area of similar habitat type supporting a similar suite of species with an estimated acreage, plus the procedure that will ensure high-quality habitat is targeted.

Applications must include a commitment to fund and implement management of the habitat in perpetuity consistent with the conservation needs of the species. A property may not be submitted under both the HCP Land Acquisition and Recovery Land Acquisition programs in the same fiscal year, and applications cannot be submitted to cover administrative costs alone.
grants.Primary Sector: Habitat Conservation Plans; Endangered Species Recovery; Land Acquisition and Conservation Easements; Perpetual Stewardship; State Wildlife Agencies
grants.Link to NOFO: CESCF HCP Land Acquisition on Simpler.Grants.gov; F26AS00071 Full Announcement (PDF); FY2026 CESCF At-Risk Species List (PDF)

grants.Description: California Energy Commission — Proposition 4 Distributed Electricity Backup Assets (DEBA) Grant Program
grants.Opportunity #: No solicitation number. Three related programs run under one CAL FIRE page, each with its own funding source, easement-holder requirements, and application timeline.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE). The federal track is administered by the USDA Forest Service in cooperation with CAL FIRE under 16 U.S.C. § 2103c, funded through the Land and Water Conservation Fund.
grants.Total Funding: Not published as a program-year total. Awards are made project by project against appraised interests in land.
grants.Award Range:
Not published. Eligible project costs include purchase of interests in lands, appraisals, land surveys, closing costs, establishing baseline information, title work, title insurance, conservation easement drafting, and other real estate transaction expenses, plus funds spent to facilitate donations of land or interests in land to a qualified and willing entity.

The Community Forest Program pays up to 50% of project costs against a 50% non-federal match.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Participation is entirely voluntary. Eligible properties are working forest and rangelands managed for production of forest products where traditional forest uses are maintained. A landowner may sell or transfer particular rights — development rights, public access — while retaining ownership and any use consistent with the easement and management plan.

Community Forests require full fee title acquisition and may be owned by local governments, Tribal governments, or qualified nonprofits. Public access is required and the land must be managed under a community forest plan.
grants.Deadline: Status by track, as published. Note 2026 Forest Legacy Program Capacity and Project Development Grant Solicitation is scheduled to open Sept. 8 but award amounts are only $50K-$150K.
grants.Program Focus:
Protects environmentally important forest land threatened with conversion to non-forest uses, so that it continues to provide sustainable timber production, wildlife habitat, recreation, watershed protection, open space, and carbon storage and sequestration.

CAL FIRE purchases or accepts donations of conservation easements or fee title on productive forest lands. The primary tool is the permanent Working Forest Conservation Easement, which goes beyond restricting development and conversion by concentrating on sustainable forest practices that produce economic value from the land and encourage long-term stewardship.

Projects are evaluated on four characteristics: Importance (economic, habitat, watershed, water supply, recreational, scenic, and historical or cultural benefits); Strategic Value (relationship to adjacent or nearby protected properties); Threat (exposure to development or conversion); and Readiness (extent of completed due diligence). Submitted parcels require a field review by CAL FIRE and may require review by the USDA Forest Service, the State Forest Stewardship Coordinating Committee, or other agencies.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grant funding for acquisition of conservation easements or fee title.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Varies by track. The Community Forest Program requires a 50% non-federal match. Match terms for the state and federal Forest Legacy tracks are set in the applicable solicitation.
grants.Primary Sector: Working Forest Conservation Easements; Forest Land Conservation; Timberland Retention; Watershed and Water Supply Protection; Carbon Sequestration; Land Trusts and Conservation Finance; Tribal and Community Forests
grants.Link to Solicitation: CAL FIRE Forest Legacy Grants; FY28 FLP LWCF Application (DOCX); Scoring Guidance (PDF); USFS Forest Legacy Program; CAL FIRE grants email updates

grants.Description: National Institutes of Health, NIMHD — Innovative Research to Improve Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander Health Outcomes (R34, Clinical Trial Optional)
grants.Opportunity #: RFA-MD-27-004; Assistance Listings 93.307 (Minority Health and Health Disparities Research) and 93.310 (Trans-NIH Research Support). Grants.gov opportunity 363713.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — National Institutes of Health, National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities, Division of Integrative Biological and Behavioral Sciences
grants.Award Range: Not published in the forecast; approximately 10 awards anticipated. R34 planning grants are typically modest and short-duration.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Broad. Public and private institutions of higher education, independent school districts, nonprofits with and without 501(c)(3) status, small businesses and other for-profits, and state, county, city, special district, and federally recognized Tribal governments.

Also eligible: Tribal governments other than federally recognized, eligible federal agencies, U.S. territories and possessions, faith-based and community-based organizations, regional organizations, and non-domestic (foreign) institutions.
grants.Deadline:
Forecast only — no NOFO has been issued.

Estimated post date December 16, 2026. Estimated application due date February 16, 2027. Estimated award and project start September 30, 2027. Fiscal year 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Planning grants supporting preparatory, feasibility, and pilot activities that advance intervention development or solutions-oriented etiologic studies to improve health and reduce disparities among Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander populations. NIMHD states that projects must be co-developed with community partners.

Areas of interest include formative studies identifying novel or understudied contributors to poor health outcomes and chronic disease; planning, adapting, and pilot-testing interventions for prevention, early detection, or control of maternal morbidity, infant health problems, and high-prevalence conditions; and feasibility and acceptability testing of strategies addressing behavioral risk factors and sustained behavior change.
grants.Primary Sector: Health Disparities Research; Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander Health; Community-Based Participatory Research; Intervention Development; Pilot and Feasibility Studies
